analysis: New vs the 5am brief: the 5:30am PT data dump landed — a PPI blowout (+1.3% MoM, biggest since March 2022), strong retail sales (+0.8%), in-line jobless claims (199K), and a hot Empire State (25.5). The tape's reaction is the story: futures barely moved and the 10Y yield FELL to 5.07% despite the inflation shock — the market is pricing AI-bubble risk, not repricing the Fed, and buying Treasuries as a haven. The day's dominant fresh catalyst is the Anthropic investor-day detail: Q3 revenue $16.8B, up 45-46% QoQ but sharply decelerated from Q2's 143-145%, only marginally above July's $65B annualized run rate — Barron's called it the rout-maker as chip stocks slid again (NVDA -1.8-2%, AMD -3.5%, MU -4.6% premarket). TSMC is the cleanest signal-vs-noise tell: record Q3 (NT$763.1B net profit, +69%), $52.3-54.3B Q4 guide, ~44% 2026 sales growth — and the stock still fell ~3% after a cautious CEO note. The market is de-rating AI credit/financing risk, not re-examining AI demand. CoreWeave's distressed bonds (~15% yield on the 2032s) remain the epicenter; memory (DRAM ETF -6.5% premarket, SK Hynix -11% overnight) is the second-order spillover. Single-source wrinkles from earlier (ByteDance-MediaTek chip talks, Micron Taiwan strike chatter) are still unconfirmed — treat as fragile. AAPL is the lone megacap green shoot: +0.7% on the China Daily report of Apple Intelligence approval in China. NYC Comptroller urging Anthropic to pause its IPO adds headline risk to the market's would-be bellwether. Into the open: the tension is whether the AI-credit selloff stays in neocloud/memory or drags the hyperscaler buyers — with Warsh's 11:30pm ET Bangkok speech as the last scheduled Fed word before Saturday's blackout.

community_signals.takeaway: Thread is skeptical the growth trajectory justifies a ~$2T IPO — 'was supposed to keep growing exponentially' — with debate over committed capex levels ('does this even cover the interest payments on their loans?'), managed earnings, and whether enterprise lock-in contracts will survive cheaper competitors (DeepSeek cited for commodity workloads). A useful practitioner-level counterweight to the media narrative that slowing growth kills the AI trade.

headlines.headline: September PPI rose 1.3% MoM vs 0.5% expected — the biggest monthly advance since March 2022 — and 6.3% YoY vs 5.3% expected (Barron's). Core PPI +0.7% MoM vs 0.3% expected, +5.0% YoY vs 4.4% expected. Energy +10.8% MoM; gasoline +20.3% drove roughly half the goods increase; food reversed from -0.3% to +1.2%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hotter than the hot CPI — strengthens the case for an Oct 27-28 hike (CME ~37% pre-data), yet the tape shrugged: futures barely moved and the 10Y fell to 5.07%, so AI-credit fear is overwhelming the rate story this morning.

headlines.headline: September retail sales +0.8% MoM vs 0.3% expected (ex-autos +0.9% vs 0.5% est); initial jobless claims 199K vs 200K expected (prior 197K); October Empire State manufacturing 25.5 vs 10.3 expected (prior 7.6).
headlines.why_it_matters: Strong consumer + hot factory data is hawkish on paper (keeps hike odds alive), but the market is reading it through the bubble lens: growth that doesn't ease AI-capex borrowing costs.

headlines.headline: Anthropic told investors at its private investor day — ahead of a ~$2T IPO expected next month — that Q3 revenue was $16.8B, up 45-46% QoQ but sharply decelerated from Q2's 143-145% sequential gain, and only marginally above July's $65B annualized run rate; it also claimed Q3 profitability on an adjusted basis and positive cash flow (FT/WSJ/Bloomberg). Separately, NYC Comptroller Mark Levine urged Anthropic to pause the IPO over AI safety/governance concerns.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade's new red flag — the would-be bellwether's growth is decelerating while its capex commitments are fixed; NVDA -1.8-2%, AMD -3.5%, MU -4.6%, SNDK -5.9% premarket. The IPO-pause letter adds headline risk to the IPO itself.

headlines.headline: TSMC posted record Q3 net profit of NT$763.1B (+69%, beat the NT$746.3B LSEG SmartEstimate), guided Q4 revenue of $52.3-54.3B and ~44% 2026 sales growth — but TSM is down 2-3% premarket after CEO C.C. Wei sounded a cautious note on macro uncertainty, rising component prices, and price-sensitive consumer demand.
headlines.why_it_matters: A record quarter getting sold is the cleanest read that this selloff is about AI credit/financing risk, not AI demand.

headlines.headline: Apple +0.7% premarket after a China Daily report said Tim Cook confirmed Apple Intelligence has been approved in China, with a test version expected later this month (real-time translation, writing tools, image cleanup; AI-powered Siri not in the first rollout). China's MIIT records also show the iPhone Duo foldable (China model A3721) completed its network license renewal on Sept 29.
headlines.why_it_matters: China AI approval unlocks the one growth lever AAPL hasn't had — the stock held up a day after its first $5T close. Single-source (China Daily) — treat as fragile until Apple confirms.

headlines.headline: CoreWeave down 3.5-6% premarket after a 15.5% Wednesday plunge; its 2032 bond yields sit near 15% (~78 cents on the dollar, distressed territory). Oracle -2%+ premarket after -8.8% Wednesday; SK Hynix -11% overnight; the DRAM ETF -6.5% premarket; SOXX on pace for an 8th straight down day (-12% over the last 7 sessions, longest losing streak in 11 years).
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI-credit stress is spreading from neocloud debt into memory and chips — the question into the open is whether it stays in credit or drags the megacap AI buyers too.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. Carry-forward: Oct 1 8-K disclosed 34.47M Class A units issued to J-W Energy at $26.7206 (9.25% fixed distribution, non-convertible, non-redeemable); listing moved to Texas Stock Exchange on Oct 5; Q2 (Aug 4) beat with revenue $342.15M and EPS $0.31 vs $0.28 est.; $600M 6.750% senior notes due 2035 issued in September to repay credit borrowings; Zacks lifted Q3 EPS est. to $0.21 (Oct 1); consensus Hold with $29.50 target.
